documentation-index.notes: Blockquote directing readers to the documentation index llms.txt. Navigation/meta only.

extend-claude-code.notes: H1 + subtitle. Introduces the extension layer concept: CLAUDE.md, Skills, subagents, hooks, MCP, plugins.

claude-code-combines-a-model.notes: Opening paragraph: built-in tools cover most tasks; this guide covers the extension layer for customization, external services, and automation.

new-to-claude-code.notes: Tip to start with CLAUDE.md for project conventions before adding other extensions.

overview.notes: H2 section intro. Lists seven extension types and their roles in the agentic loop.

overview-extension-list.notes: Bullet list: CLAUDE.md, Skills, MCP, Subagents, Agent teams, Hooks, Plugins/marketplaces. Each mapped to their function.

skills-are-the-most-flexible.notes: Skills described as most flexible extension: markdown file, invocable with slash command or auto-loaded, can run in current conversation or isolated context via subagents.

match-features-to-your-goal.notes: H2 intro: features range from always-on to on-demand to event-driven automation.

match-features-table.notes: Feature comparison table: CLAUDE.md, Skill, Subagent, Agent teams, MCP, Hook — with what each does, when to use, and example.

plugins-are-the-packaging-layer.notes: Plugins bundle skills, hooks, subagents, MCP servers. Plugin skills are namespaced to avoid conflicts.

build-your-setup-over-time.notes: H3 intro: no need to configure everything upfront; features have recognizable triggers.

build-your-setup-trigger-table.notes: Trigger table: maps common pain points to the correct extension type (CLAUDE.md, skill, MCP, subagent, hook, plugin).

same-triggers-update.notes: Note that the same triggers apply to updating existing features: repeated mistakes signal CLAUDE.md edits, tweaked workflows signal skill revisions.

compare-similar-features.notes: H3 intro to tabbed comparison section.

skill-vs-subagent-tab.notes: Tab: Skills are reusable content; subagents are isolated workers. Comparison table covers what it is, key benefit, best for. Notes: subagent can preload skills via `skills:` field; skill can use `context: fork`.

claude-md-vs-skill-tab.notes: Tab: Both store instructions but load differently. CLAUDE.md: every session automatically. Skills: on demand. Rule of thumb: keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines.

claude-md-vs-rules-vs-skills-tab.notes: Tab: Three-way comparison. rules/ files can be scoped to file paths with `paths` frontmatter, loading only when matching files are opened.

subagent-vs-agent-team-tab.notes: Tab: Subagents report to main context only; agent teams communicate peer-to-peer with shared task list. Agent teams cost more (separate Claude instances). Agent teams experimental and disabled by default — caveat.

agent-teams-experimental-note.notes: Note block: Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default.

mcp-vs-skill-tab.notes: Tab: MCP provides tool/data access to external services; skills provide knowledge and workflows. They complement each other — MCP gives the connection, skill teaches how to use it.

understand-how-features-layer.notes: H3: Features can be defined at multiple levels (user-wide, per-project, plugins, managed policies).

layering-bullet-list.notes: CLAUDE.md is additive across all levels. Skills/subagents override by name with priority order (managed > user > project for skills; managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin for subagents). MCP overrides by name (local > project > user). Hooks merge: all fire for matching events.

combine-features.notes: H3: Each extension solves a different problem; real setups combine them.

combine-features-table.notes: Pattern table: Skill+MCP, Skill+Subagent, CLAUDE.md+Skills, Hook+MCP. Shows how features combine in practice.

understand-context-costs.notes: H2: Every feature consumes context. Too much can fill the window or degrade effectiveness (skills may not trigger correctly). Links to Explore the context window.

context-cost-by-feature.notes: H3 intro: each feature has a different loading strategy and context cost.

context-cost-table.notes: Table: CLAUDE.md (full content every request), Skills (descriptions at start + full on use), MCP (tool names at start), Subagents (isolated from main), Hooks (zero unless returns context).

disable-model-invocation-footnote.notes: Footnote: `disable-model-invocation: true` hides skill from Claude until manually invoked, reducing context cost to zero.

understand-how-features-load.notes: H3 intro to tabbed per-feature loading details. Includes context-loading diagram.

context-loading-diagram.notes: Diagram showing when each feature loads relative to session lifecycle.

claude-md-load-tab.notes: Tab: Loads at session start. Full content of all CLAUDE.md files (managed, user, project). Nested files discovered as subdirectories are accessed. Tip: keep under 200 lines.

skills-load-tab.notes: Tab: Descriptions load at session start; full content when used. `disable-model-invocation: true` = nothing loads until invoked. In subagents, skills are fully preloaded at launch rather than on-demand; subagents don't inherit skills from main session — must be specified explicitly.

mcp-servers-load-tab.notes: Tab: Tool names at session start; schemas deferred. MCP connections can fail silently — tools disappear without warning. Check with `/mcp`. Reliability caveat.

subagents-load-tab.notes: Tab: On demand. Fresh isolated context: system prompt (shared with parent for cache efficiency), full content of `skills:` field, CLAUDE.md + git status inherited from parent, context passed by lead agent. Does not inherit conversation history or invoked skills.

hooks-load-tab.notes: Tab: Fire at lifecycle events (tool execution, session boundaries, prompt submission, permission requests, compaction). Run as external scripts. Zero context cost unless hook returns output.

learn-more.notes: H2: Card group navigation links to individual feature guides. Navigation only.
